misconception.description: averaging the two contribution margins without weighting them by how many of each product is sold, which ignores the sales mix

worked_example.text: A cafe sells coffees at a margin of EUR 2 and cakes at a margin of EUR 5, and sells four coffees for every cake. Its fixed costs are EUR 26,000 a month.
worked_example.solution: Weighted average margin = (4 x 2 + 1 x 5) / 5 = 13 / 5 = EUR 2.60 per item. Break-even = 26,000 / 2.60 = 10,000 items a month, of which 8,000 coffees and 2,000 cakes.

problem.text: A shop sells two products. Product A sells for EUR 30 with a variable cost of EUR 10; product B sells for EUR 50 with a variable cost of EUR 40. The shop sells three units of A for every unit of B, and its fixed costs are EUR 105,000 a year. How many units in total must it sell to break even?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: a plain average of the two margins, as if the shop sold equal numbers of each
using only the better margin, as if the shop sold nothing but product A

hints: With two products there is no single contribution margin, so the first job is to build one that represents the mix the shop actually sells.
Work out the margin on each product, then weight them: for every four units sold, three are A and one is B, so A's margin should count three times as heavily.
Divide the fixed costs by that weighted average margin to get the total number of units, then split them back into A and B in the same three-to-one proportion.
worked_solution: Step 1: the margins are 30 - 10 = EUR 20 on A and 50 - 40 = EUR 10 on B. Step 2: weight them by the mix. In every batch of four units, three are A and one is B, so the average unit contributes (3 x 20 + 1 x 10) / 4 = 70 / 4 = EUR 17.50. Step 3: divide the fixed costs by that figure: 105,000 / 17.50 = 6,000 units in total, made up of 4,500 of A and 1,500 of B. A plain average of the two margins would give EUR 15 and 7,000 units, overstating the requirement because it pretends the shop sells as many of the thin-margin product as of the fat one.

near_transfer.text: The same shop, selling three units of A for every unit of B and breaking even at 6,000 units in total, wants to know the split. How many units of product A does it need to sell?

distractors.note: splitting the total evenly, ignoring the three-to-one mix
reporting the units of B instead of the units of A

far_transfer.text: The same shop sells product A at EUR 30 and product B at EUR 50, three units of A for every unit of B. What is the weighted average selling price of a unit?

distractors.note: a plain average, ignoring that three times as many of the cheaper product are sold
the weights applied to the wrong products
